profile.purpose: A one-year long-term review of Blundstone Chelsea boots in rustic brown nubuck, covering wear, break-in and work versus fashion use, with a pond-standing water resistance test.
profile.thesis: After about a year of near-daily wear, including hikes, runs and city walking, the Blundstones are judged to be performing about as expected for their price. The creator weighs their scuffing, nubuck leather, break-in and place as a work-versus-fashion boot, then tests how long the untreated boots keep water out.
key_takeaways: Worn almost daily for about eight months, including hikes in Maine, daily two-mile runs for about four months and 10,000 steps a day.
The leather is described as decent, about as thick as Birkenstock straps; the interior is soft and the treads are fine after a year.
Scuffs are heavier than expected, partly blamed on kicking rocks while descending mountains and on the distressed nubuck finish.
He says he would choose a smoother leather next time because it holds protection better than sanded nubuck.
The elastic side panels are slightly looser but still hold the boot on.
Break-in blisters appeared when he started running and walking track in them and stopped after two to three weeks.
He sees Blundstone as having shifted from work boot toward fashion boot, compared with Carhartt and Carhartt WIP.
In a pond test, with boots untreated for about a year, his feet stayed mostly dry; only the elastic band area got slightly wet.

outline.title: Intro and Comment Responses
outline.summary: Responds to comments on his first Blundstone video, including that the boots are injection molded and that better boots exist in this style. Says they look great after a year.

outline.title: How They Were Worn
outline.summary: Describes a year of wear: daily use for about eight months, hikes in Maine despite little ankle support, and daily runs and walks to fade his jeans.

outline.title: After a Year They Look Great
outline.summary: Overall condition relative to price: leather quality and thickness, soft inner leather, fine treads, and what he expects over the coming years.

outline.title: Scuffs, Elastics and Interior Wear
outline.summary: Covers scuffing from mountain descents, elastics that are slightly looser but still tight, the footbed imprint, and lining wearing at the big toe.

outline.title: Nubuck vs Smooth Leather
outline.summary: Explains why the sanded, artificially aged rustic nubuck shows wear more and why he would pick a smoother leather.

outline.title: Break-In and Blisters
outline.summary: Describes getting break-in blisters once he started running and walking track in the boots, which stopped after two to three weeks.

outline.title: Work Boot or Fashion Boot
outline.summary: Discusses Blundstone's manufacturing history and its shift into a fashion boot, compared with Carhartt and Carhartt WIP. Concludes it is decent but not exceptional for work and fits casual everyday wear.

outline.title: Water Resistance Test
outline.summary: With the boots untreated for a year, he plans an ocean test but instead stands in a local pond to see how long his feet stay dry, including submerging the elastic bands.

outline.title: Final Verdict
outline.summary: Concludes the boots are fine for crossing streams or standing in mud and remain great after a year.

outline.title: Childhood Swing Story
outline.summary: A closing personal anecdote about growing up near the swings and his old school.
